Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Agribusiness 120,000 jobs from palm oil project within 2 years sounds unrealistic – Stephen Amoah Source : Emma Ankrah 19 November 2026 7:06pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Member of Parliament for Nhyaieso and former Deputy Finance Minister, Dr Stephen Amoah, has questioned the government's claim that its palm oil project has created 120,000 jobs within two years.
He says the government must provide further details about the project, including the size of land involved, its stage of implementation and the nature of the jobs being counted.
Speaking on Joy FM's Top Story on Thursday, November 19, Dr Amoah said, given his experience as a palm plantation farmer, he finds it difficult to understand how such a large number of jobs could have been generated within the period.
“I would be surprised that in two years there is a palm plantation project in Ghana here that has employed 120,000. I can't say he's lying, because I'm not there. But it doesn't really, really sound realistic,” he said.
He challenged Presidential Spokesperson Felix Kwakye Ofosu to explain whether the project had reached the planting or production stage, or was still at the land-clearing stage.
Dr Amoah also demanded clarity on whether the figures cover permanent or temporary employment, the skills composition of the workforce and the entities responsible for paying the workers.
He further questioned the government's contribution to the project and the private-sector companies involved.
His comments follow claims by Mr Kwakye Ofosu that the government's 24-hour economy programme is expanding operations across several sectors, including filling stations, fuel depots, refineries, factories and public offices.
Dr Amoah has separately argued that the 24-hour economy the NDC promised, centred on establishing factories and industries capable of operating around the clock and creating large-scale employment, has yet to begin.
